source_notes: Direct O’Connor 2005 preparation at pH 10.0 and room temperature is separate from the cited Rogach 1999 base procedure at pH 11.2.
Rogach 1999 precursor charges, nitrogen bubbling duration, H2Te-generator inputs and concentration step are cited context only; unchanged inheritance by O’Connor is not confirmed.
HRTEM/XRD product association is article-level. A coded batch or aliquot identity is not reported.
Figure 2 is assigned to downstream array and device specimens; it does not add a synthesis variant or prove exact batch lineage.
Publisher permission for rehosting both source-figure crops remains unverified.

No coded batch/aliquot link is reported across solution optical, HRTEM, XRD, deposited array and device measurements.
No named geometric morphology, refined unit-cell parameters or atomic-coordinate CIF is reported in this source.
SI identity/content and publisher permission for figure reuse are unverified.

items.title: O’Connor 2005 pH 10.0 aqueous HgTe quantum-dot adaptation
items.summary: O’Connor directly identifies aqueous mercury(II) perchlorate, 1-thioglycerol, N2-saturated solution and H2Te gas. Initial precursor/stabilizer amounts and gas dose are not reported. See the cited 1999 method in a separate, non-inherited context.

items.title: O’Connor 2005 pH 10.0 aqueous HgTe quantum-dot adaptation
items.summary: At room temperature, prepare the reported aqueous Hg(II) perchlorate/1-thioglycerol mixture at pH 10.0, saturate with N2, pass H2Te through, add propan-2-ol dropwise to turbidity, stir 2–3 h, centrifuge at 6000 rpm for 10 min, then redisperse in 500 µL water OR DMF with 2.5 µL 1-thioglycerol. Recipe amounts omitted by the source remain unknown.

items.title: Near-infrared device context
items.summary: The article studies HgTe quantum-dot arrays for near-infrared electroluminescence. The solution PL, deposited-array PL and device EL are distinct measurement contexts; their wavelengths should not be treated as one spectrum or one aliquot.

items.title: Water-limited solution emission window
items.summary: The source discusses a water-reabsorption feature near 1150 nm and an absorption cutoff near 1450 nm in the aqueous optical context. This is an article interpretation, not a general material constant.
